facts.text: The library is for flying real CrazyFlie 2.x drones, with a simulation environment via PyFlyt
The upstream README says the library is in the developmental stage
The hardware example opens a DroneController on a radio URI, selects position control, starts it, sends a hover setpoint at 0.5 m and then 0 m, stops it and ends it
The hardware example sends the setpoint [0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.0] to hover at 0.5 m
The setpoint is four numbers: (x, y, z, yaw) in position control or (vx, vy, vz, vyaw) in velocity control
The control thread repeats every period = 1/40.0 s
With running true, the control thread sends a position setpoint when pos_control is true and a world-frame velocity setpoint otherwise
The control thread multiplies the four-value setpoint by self.rad_to_deg before sending it
rad_to_deg is [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, math.pi / 180.0], so only the fourth value is converted from radians to degrees and the first three are passed unchanged
When running is false the control thread calls send_stop_setpoint every period
start() sets running true, stop() sets running false, and end() clears running, stops the logging configuration and closes the link
position_estimate holds the logged stateEstimate.x, .y and .z and the yaw converted from degrees to radians
position_estimate and setpoint are four-element numpy arrays initialised to zero
The velocity example describes the setpoint [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0] as flying in horizontal x with a 1 rad/s yaw rate
The constructor opens a SyncCrazyflie link and starts a daemon control thread
